items.title: Regulation of Blood Flow in Capillaries

source_refs.note: Regulation of Blood Flow in Capillaries: a main subheading of 11.2 Blood vessels, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 244-244.

blocks.text: The amount of blood flowing in capillaries is controlled by constricting or dilating the capillaries. Nervous stimulation can constrict capillaries and certain chemicals such as histamine can dilate them. Some capillaries are connected with arterioles and venules through loops of other capillaries. The entry of each loop is guarded by a ring of muscles called a pre-capillary sphincter. These sphincters regulate the amount of blood flowing through capillaries.

blocks.alt: An arteriole across the top and a venule across the bottom, joined by six capillary loops that are red near the arteriole and blue near the venule. A ring-shaped pre-capillary sphincter sits where each loop leaves the arteriole.
